قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الرَّسُولُ لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ في الكُفْرِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنّا بِأفْواهِهِمْ ولَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي بِهِ المُنافِقِينَ المُظْهِرِينَ لِلْإيمانِ المُبْطِنِينَ لِلْكُفْرِ.

﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي اليَهُودَ.

﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ لِيَكْذِبُوا عَلَيْكَ عِنْدَهم إذا أتَوْا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، والزَّجّاجِ.

(p-39) والثّانِي: أنَّ مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ أيْ قائِلُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ عَلَيْكَ.

وَ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ يَعْنِي في قِصَّةِ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ مِنَ اليَهُودِ الَّذِي حَكَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَأنْكَرُوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ مِن بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم إذا سَمِعُوا كَلامَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ غَيَّرُوهُ بِالكَذِبِ عَلَيْهِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: هو تَغْيِيرُ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ تَعالى في جَلْدِ الزّانِي بَدَلًا مِن رَجْمِهِ، وقِيلَ في إسْقاطِ القَوَدِ (القِصاصِ) عِنْدَ اسْتِحْقاقِهِ.

﴿يَقُولُونَ إنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذا فَخُذُوهُ وإنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فاحْذَرُوا﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: «أنَّهُ يُرِيدُ بِذَلِكَ حِينَ زَنى رَجُلٌ مِنهم بِامْرَأةٍ فَأنْفَذُوهُ إلى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهم وقالُوا: إنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالجَلْدِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالرَّجْمِ فَلا تَقْبَلُوهُ، فَقامَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إلى مَدارِسِ تَوْراتِهِمْ وفِيها أحْبارُهم يَتْلُونَ التَّوْراةَ، فَأتى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ صُورِيّا، وكانَ أعْوَرَ، وهو مِن أعْلَمِهِمْ فَقالَ لَهُ أسْألُكَ بِالَّذِي أنْزَلَ التَّوْراةَ بِطُورِ سَيْناءَ عَلى مُوسى بْنِ عِمْرانَ هَلْ في التَّوْراةِ الرَّجْمُ؟ فَأمْسَكَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلْ بِهِ حَتّى اعْتَرَفَ، فَأمَرَ بِهِما النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فَرُجِما، قالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: وكُنْتُ فِيمَن رَجَمَهُ وأنَّهُ لَيَقِيها الأحْجارَ بِنَفْسِهِ حَتّى ماتَتْ»، ثُمَّ إنَّ ابْنَ صُورِيّا أنْكَرَ وفِيهِ أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وجابِرٍ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ المُسَيِّبِ، والسُّدِّيِّ، وابْنِ زَيْدٍ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ في قَتِيلٍ مِنهم، قالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: قَتَلَتْ بَنُو النَّضِيرِ رَجُلًا مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وكانُوا يَمْتَنِعُونَ بِالِاسْتِطالَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ القَوَدِ بِالدِّيَةِ، وإذا قَتَلَتْ بَنُو قُرَيْظَةَ مِنهم رَجُلًا لَمْ يَقْنَعُوا إلّا بِالقَوَدِ دُونَ الدِّيَةِ، قالُوا: إنْ أفْتاكم بِالدِّيَةِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ أفْتاكم بِالقَوَدِ فَرُدُّوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

﴿وَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُها: عَذابُهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: إضْلالُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

(p-40) والثّالِثُ: فَضِيحَتُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ الزَّجّاجِ.

﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الضِّيقِ والحَرَجِ عُقُوبَةً لَهم.

والثّانِي: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الكُفْرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أكّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾ فِيهِ أرْبَعَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ السُّحْتَ الرِّشْوَةُ، وهو مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ الرِّشْوَةُ في الحُكْمِ، وهو قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ.

والثّالِثُ: هو الِاسْتِعْجالُ في القَضِيَّةِ، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ.

والرّابِعُ: ما فِيهِ الغارُّ مِنَ الأثْمانِ المُحَرَّمَةِ: كَثَمَنِ الكَلْبِ، والخِنْزِيرِ، والخَمْرِ وعَسَبِ الفَحْلِ، وحُلْوانِ الكاهِنِ.

وَأصْلُ السُّحْتِ الِاسْتِئْصالُ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَيُسْحِتَكم بِعَذابٍ﴾ أيْ يَسْتَأْصِلُكم، وقالَ الفَرَزْدَقُ:

وعَضُّ زَمانٍ يا ابْنَ مَرْوانَ لَمْ يَدَعْ مِنَ المالِ إلّا مُسْحِتًا أوْ مُجْلِفْ

فَسُمِّيَ سُحْتًا لِأنَّهُ يَسْحَتُ الدِّينَ والمُرُوءَةَ.

﴿فَإنْ جاءُوكَ فاحْكم بَيْنَهم أوْ أعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ فِيمَن أُرِيدَ بِذَلِكَ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اليَهُودِيّانِ اللَّذانِ زَنَيا، خُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُما بِالرَّجْمِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، والزُّهْرِيِّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّها في نَفْسَيْنِ مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وبَنِي النَّضِيرِ قَتَلَ أحَدُهُما صاحِبَهُ، فَخُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ عِنْدَ احْتِكامِهِما إلَيْهِ بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بِالقَوَدِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

(p-41) واخْتَلَفُوا في التَّخْيِيرِ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَهم، هَلْ هو ثابِتٌ أوْ مَنسُوخٌ؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ ثابِتٌ، وأنَّ كُلَّ حاكِمٍ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ مُخَيَّرٌ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَ أهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ (أهْلِ العَهْدِ مِن غَيْرِ المُسْلِمِينَ في دارِ الإسْلامِ) بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ، وقَتادَةَ، وعَطاءٍ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ مَنسُوخٌ (أي بالنسخ: رفع الحكم بدليل متأخر)، وأنَّ الحُكْمَ بَيْنَهم واجِبٌ عَلى مَن تَحاكَمُوا إلَيْهِ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وعُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ العَزِيزِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، وقَدْ نَسَخَهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنِ احْكم بَيْنَهم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ فِيها حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالرَّجْمِ.

والثّانِي: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالقَوَدِ.

﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: بَعْدَ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ في التَّوْراةِ.

والثّانِي: بَعْدَ تَحْكِيمِكَ.

﴿وَما أُولَئِكَ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أيْ في تَحْكِيمِكَ، أنَّهُ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ، مَعَ جُحُودِهِمْ نُبُوَّتَكَ.

والثّانِي: يَعْنِي في تَوَلِّيهِمْ عَنْ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ غَيْرَ راضِينَ بِهِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنّا أنْزَلْنا التَّوْراةَ فِيها هُدًى ونُورٌ﴾ يَعْنِي بِالهُدى الدَّلِيلُ.

وَبِالنُّورِ البَيانُ.

﴿يَحْكُمُ بِها النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أسْلَمُوا﴾ فِيهِمْ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم جَماعَةُ أنْبِياءَ مِنهم مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ. والثّانِي: المُرادُ نَبِيُّنا مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ وحْدَهُ وإنْ ذُكِرَ بِلَفْظِ الجَمْعِ.

(p-42) وَفِي الَّذِي يَحْكُمُ بِهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أرادَ رَجْمَ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ، والقَوَدَ مِنَ القاتِلِ العامِدِ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّهُ الحُكْمُ بِجَمِيعِ ما فِيها مِن غَيْرِ تَخْصِيصٍ، ما لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَسْخٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى الَّذِينَ هادُوا، وهُمُ اليَهُودُ، وفي جَوازِ الحُكْمِ بِها عَلى غَيْرِ اليَهُودِ وجْهانِ، عَلى اخْتِلافِهِمْ في التِزامِنا شَرائِعَ مَن قَبْلَنا إذا لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَصٌّ يَنْسَخُ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿والرَّبّانِيُّونَ والأحْبارُ﴾ واحِدُ الأحْبارِ حَبْرٌ بِالفَتْحِ، قالَ الفَرّاءُ: أكْثَرُ ما سَمِعْتُ حِبْرٌ بِالكَسْرِ، وهو العالِمُ، سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ اشْتِقاقًا مِنَ التَّحْبِيرِ، وهو التَّحْسِينُ، لِأنَّ العالِمَ يُحَسِّنُ الحَسَنَ ويُقَبِّحُ القَبِيحَ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ لِأنَّ العِلْمَ في نَفْسِهِ حَسَنٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ يَحْكُمُونَ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ والعُلَماءُ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

وَفي ﴿اسْتُحْفِظُوا﴾ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اسْتُودِعُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الأخْفَشِ.

والثّانِي: العِلْمُ بِما حَفِظُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الكَلْبِيِّ.

﴿وَكانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَداءَ﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى حُكْمِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أنَّهُ في التَّوْراةِ.

﴿فَلا تَخْشَوُا النّاسَ واخْشَوْنِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: فَلا تَخْشَوْهم في كِتْمانِ ما أنْزَلْتُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

والثّانِي: في الحُكْمِ بِما أنْزَلْتُ.

﴿وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِآياتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا﴾ فِيهِ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى كِتْمانِها أجْرًا.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى تَعْلِيمِها أجْرًا.

(p-43) ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكافِرُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾. وفي اخْتِلافِ هَذِهِ الآيِ الثَّلاثِ أرْبَعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّها وارِدَةٌ في اليَهُودِ دُونَ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وحُذَيْفَةَ، والبَراءِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ.

الثّانِي: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في أهْلِ الكِتابِ، وحُكْمُها عامٌّ في جَمِيعِ النّاسِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ أرادَ بِالكافِرِينَ أهْلَ الإسْلامِ، وبِالظّالِمِينَ اليَهُودَ، وبِالفاسِقِينَ النَّصارى، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّ مَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ جاحِدًا بِهِ، فَهو كافِرٌ، ومَن لَمْ يَحْكم مُقِرًّا بِهِ فَهو ظالِمٌ فاسِقٌ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الرَّسُولُ لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ في الكُفْرِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنّا بِأفْواهِهِمْ ولَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي بِهِ المُنافِقِينَ المُظْهِرِينَ لِلْإيمانِ المُبْطِنِينَ لِلْكُفْرِ.

﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي اليَهُودَ.

﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ لِيَكْذِبُوا عَلَيْكَ عِنْدَهم إذا أتَوْا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، والزَّجّاجِ.

(p-39) والثّانِي: أنَّ مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ أيْ قائِلُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ عَلَيْكَ.

وَ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ يَعْنِي في قِصَّةِ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ مِنَ اليَهُودِ الَّذِي حَكَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَأنْكَرُوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ مِن بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم إذا سَمِعُوا كَلامَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ غَيَّرُوهُ بِالكَذِبِ عَلَيْهِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: هو تَغْيِيرُ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ تَعالى في جَلْدِ الزّانِي بَدَلًا مِن رَجْمِهِ، وقِيلَ في إسْقاطِ القَوَدِ (القِصاصِ) عِنْدَ اسْتِحْقاقِهِ.

﴿يَقُولُونَ إنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذا فَخُذُوهُ وإنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فاحْذَرُوا﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: «أنَّهُ يُرِيدُ بِذَلِكَ حِينَ زَنى رَجُلٌ مِنهم بِامْرَأةٍ فَأنْفَذُوهُ إلى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهم وقالُوا: إنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالجَلْدِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالرَّجْمِ فَلا تَقْبَلُوهُ، فَقامَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إلى مَدارِسِ تَوْراتِهِمْ وفِيها أحْبارُهم يَتْلُونَ التَّوْراةَ، فَأتى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ صُورِيّا، وكانَ أعْوَرَ، وهو مِن أعْلَمِهِمْ فَقالَ لَهُ أسْألُكَ بِالَّذِي أنْزَلَ التَّوْراةَ بِطُورِ سَيْناءَ عَلى مُوسى بْنِ عِمْرانَ هَلْ في التَّوْراةِ الرَّجْمُ؟ فَأمْسَكَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلْ بِهِ حَتّى اعْتَرَفَ، فَأمَرَ بِهِما النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فَرُجِما، قالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: وكُنْتُ فِيمَن رَجَمَهُ وأنَّهُ لَيَقِيها الأحْجارَ بِنَفْسِهِ حَتّى ماتَتْ»، ثُمَّ إنَّ ابْنَ صُورِيّا أنْكَرَ وفِيهِ أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وجابِرٍ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ المُسَيِّبِ، والسُّدِّيِّ، وابْنِ زَيْدٍ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ في قَتِيلٍ مِنهم، قالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: قَتَلَتْ بَنُو النَّضِيرِ رَجُلًا مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وكانُوا يَمْتَنِعُونَ بِالِاسْتِطالَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ القَوَدِ بِالدِّيَةِ، وإذا قَتَلَتْ بَنُو قُرَيْظَةَ مِنهم رَجُلًا لَمْ يَقْنَعُوا إلّا بِالقَوَدِ دُونَ الدِّيَةِ، قالُوا: إنْ أفْتاكم بِالدِّيَةِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ أفْتاكم بِالقَوَدِ فَرُدُّوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

﴿وَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُها: عَذابُهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: إضْلالُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

(p-40) والثّالِثُ: فَضِيحَتُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ الزَّجّاجِ.

﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الضِّيقِ والحَرَجِ عُقُوبَةً لَهم.

والثّانِي: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الكُفْرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أكّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾ فِيهِ أرْبَعَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ السُّحْتَ الرِّشْوَةُ، وهو مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ الرِّشْوَةُ في الحُكْمِ، وهو قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ.

والثّالِثُ: هو الِاسْتِعْجالُ في القَضِيَّةِ، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ.

والرّابِعُ: ما فِيهِ الغارُّ مِنَ الأثْمانِ المُحَرَّمَةِ: كَثَمَنِ الكَلْبِ، والخِنْزِيرِ، والخَمْرِ وعَسَبِ الفَحْلِ، وحُلْوانِ الكاهِنِ.

وَأصْلُ السُّحْتِ الِاسْتِئْصالُ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَيُسْحِتَكم بِعَذابٍ﴾ أيْ يَسْتَأْصِلُكم، وقالَ الفَرَزْدَقُ:

وعَضُّ زَمانٍ يا ابْنَ مَرْوانَ لَمْ يَدَعْ مِنَ المالِ إلّا مُسْحِتًا أوْ مُجْلِفْ

فَسُمِّيَ سُحْتًا لِأنَّهُ يَسْحَتُ الدِّينَ والمُرُوءَةَ.

﴿فَإنْ جاءُوكَ فاحْكم بَيْنَهم أوْ أعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ فِيمَن أُرِيدَ بِذَلِكَ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اليَهُودِيّانِ اللَّذانِ زَنَيا، خُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُما بِالرَّجْمِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، والزُّهْرِيِّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّها في نَفْسَيْنِ مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وبَنِي النَّضِيرِ قَتَلَ أحَدُهُما صاحِبَهُ، فَخُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ عِنْدَ احْتِكامِهِما إلَيْهِ بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بِالقَوَدِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

(p-41) واخْتَلَفُوا في التَّخْيِيرِ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَهم، هَلْ هو ثابِتٌ أوْ مَنسُوخٌ؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ ثابِتٌ، وأنَّ كُلَّ حاكِمٍ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ مُخَيَّرٌ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَ أهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ (أهْلِ العَهْدِ مِن غَيْرِ المُسْلِمِينَ في دارِ الإسْلامِ) بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ، وقَتادَةَ، وعَطاءٍ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ مَنسُوخٌ (أي بالنسخ: رفع الحكم بدليل متأخر)، وأنَّ الحُكْمَ بَيْنَهم واجِبٌ عَلى مَن تَحاكَمُوا إلَيْهِ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وعُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ العَزِيزِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، وقَدْ نَسَخَهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنِ احْكم بَيْنَهم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ فِيها حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالرَّجْمِ.

والثّانِي: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالقَوَدِ.

﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: بَعْدَ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ في التَّوْراةِ.

والثّانِي: بَعْدَ تَحْكِيمِكَ.

﴿وَما أُولَئِكَ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أيْ في تَحْكِيمِكَ، أنَّهُ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ، مَعَ جُحُودِهِمْ نُبُوَّتَكَ.

والثّانِي: يَعْنِي في تَوَلِّيهِمْ عَنْ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ غَيْرَ راضِينَ بِهِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنّا أنْزَلْنا التَّوْراةَ فِيها هُدًى ونُورٌ﴾ يَعْنِي بِالهُدى الدَّلِيلُ.

وَبِالنُّورِ البَيانُ.

﴿يَحْكُمُ بِها النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أسْلَمُوا﴾ فِيهِمْ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم جَماعَةُ أنْبِياءَ مِنهم مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ. والثّانِي: المُرادُ نَبِيُّنا مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ وحْدَهُ وإنْ ذُكِرَ بِلَفْظِ الجَمْعِ.

(p-42) وَفِي الَّذِي يَحْكُمُ بِهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أرادَ رَجْمَ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ، والقَوَدَ مِنَ القاتِلِ العامِدِ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّهُ الحُكْمُ بِجَمِيعِ ما فِيها مِن غَيْرِ تَخْصِيصٍ، ما لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَسْخٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى الَّذِينَ هادُوا، وهُمُ اليَهُودُ، وفي جَوازِ الحُكْمِ بِها عَلى غَيْرِ اليَهُودِ وجْهانِ، عَلى اخْتِلافِهِمْ في التِزامِنا شَرائِعَ مَن قَبْلَنا إذا لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَصٌّ يَنْسَخُ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿والرَّبّانِيُّونَ والأحْبارُ﴾ واحِدُ الأحْبارِ حَبْرٌ بِالفَتْحِ، قالَ الفَرّاءُ: أكْثَرُ ما سَمِعْتُ حِبْرٌ بِالكَسْرِ، وهو العالِمُ، سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ اشْتِقاقًا مِنَ التَّحْبِيرِ، وهو التَّحْسِينُ، لِأنَّ العالِمَ يُحَسِّنُ الحَسَنَ ويُقَبِّحُ القَبِيحَ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ لِأنَّ العِلْمَ في نَفْسِهِ حَسَنٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ يَحْكُمُونَ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ والعُلَماءُ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

وَفي ﴿اسْتُحْفِظُوا﴾ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اسْتُودِعُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الأخْفَشِ.

والثّانِي: العِلْمُ بِما حَفِظُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الكَلْبِيِّ.

﴿وَكانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَداءَ﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى حُكْمِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أنَّهُ في التَّوْراةِ.

﴿فَلا تَخْشَوُا النّاسَ واخْشَوْنِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: فَلا تَخْشَوْهم في كِتْمانِ ما أنْزَلْتُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

والثّانِي: في الحُكْمِ بِما أنْزَلْتُ.

﴿وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِآياتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا﴾ فِيهِ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى كِتْمانِها أجْرًا.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى تَعْلِيمِها أجْرًا.

(p-43) ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكافِرُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾. وفي اخْتِلافِ هَذِهِ الآيِ الثَّلاثِ أرْبَعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّها وارِدَةٌ في اليَهُودِ دُونَ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وحُذَيْفَةَ، والبَراءِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ.

الثّانِي: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في أهْلِ الكِتابِ، وحُكْمُها عامٌّ في جَمِيعِ النّاسِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ أرادَ بِالكافِرِينَ أهْلَ الإسْلامِ، وبِالظّالِمِينَ اليَهُودَ، وبِالفاسِقِينَ النَّصارى، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّ مَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ جاحِدًا بِهِ، فَهو كافِرٌ، ومَن لَمْ يَحْكم مُقِرًّا بِهِ فَهو ظالِمٌ فاسِقٌ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الرَّسُولُ لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ في الكُفْرِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنّا بِأفْواهِهِمْ ولَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي بِهِ المُنافِقِينَ المُظْهِرِينَ لِلْإيمانِ المُبْطِنِينَ لِلْكُفْرِ.

﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي اليَهُودَ.

﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ لِيَكْذِبُوا عَلَيْكَ عِنْدَهم إذا أتَوْا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، والزَّجّاجِ.

(p-39) والثّانِي: أنَّ مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ أيْ قائِلُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ عَلَيْكَ.

وَ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ يَعْنِي في قِصَّةِ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ مِنَ اليَهُودِ الَّذِي حَكَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَأنْكَرُوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ مِن بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم إذا سَمِعُوا كَلامَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ غَيَّرُوهُ بِالكَذِبِ عَلَيْهِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: هو تَغْيِيرُ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ تَعالى في جَلْدِ الزّانِي بَدَلًا مِن رَجْمِهِ، وقِيلَ في إسْقاطِ القَوَدِ (القِصاصِ) عِنْدَ اسْتِحْقاقِهِ.

﴿يَقُولُونَ إنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذا فَخُذُوهُ وإنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فاحْذَرُوا﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: «أنَّهُ يُرِيدُ بِذَلِكَ حِينَ زَنى رَجُلٌ مِنهم بِامْرَأةٍ فَأنْفَذُوهُ إلى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهم وقالُوا: إنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالجَلْدِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالرَّجْمِ فَلا تَقْبَلُوهُ، فَقامَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إلى مَدارِسِ تَوْراتِهِمْ وفِيها أحْبارُهم يَتْلُونَ التَّوْراةَ، فَأتى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ صُورِيّا، وكانَ أعْوَرَ، وهو مِن أعْلَمِهِمْ فَقالَ لَهُ أسْألُكَ بِالَّذِي أنْزَلَ التَّوْراةَ بِطُورِ سَيْناءَ عَلى مُوسى بْنِ عِمْرانَ هَلْ في التَّوْراةِ الرَّجْمُ؟ فَأمْسَكَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلْ بِهِ حَتّى اعْتَرَفَ، فَأمَرَ بِهِما النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فَرُجِما، قالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: وكُنْتُ فِيمَن رَجَمَهُ وأنَّهُ لَيَقِيها الأحْجارَ بِنَفْسِهِ حَتّى ماتَتْ»، ثُمَّ إنَّ ابْنَ صُورِيّا أنْكَرَ وفِيهِ أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وجابِرٍ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ المُسَيِّبِ، والسُّدِّيِّ، وابْنِ زَيْدٍ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ في قَتِيلٍ مِنهم، قالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: قَتَلَتْ بَنُو النَّضِيرِ رَجُلًا مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وكانُوا يَمْتَنِعُونَ بِالِاسْتِطالَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ القَوَدِ بِالدِّيَةِ، وإذا قَتَلَتْ بَنُو قُرَيْظَةَ مِنهم رَجُلًا لَمْ يَقْنَعُوا إلّا بِالقَوَدِ دُونَ الدِّيَةِ، قالُوا: إنْ أفْتاكم بِالدِّيَةِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ أفْتاكم بِالقَوَدِ فَرُدُّوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

﴿وَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُها: عَذابُهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: إضْلالُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

(p-40) والثّالِثُ: فَضِيحَتُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ الزَّجّاجِ.

﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الضِّيقِ والحَرَجِ عُقُوبَةً لَهم.

والثّانِي: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الكُفْرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أكّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾ فِيهِ أرْبَعَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ السُّحْتَ الرِّشْوَةُ، وهو مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ الرِّشْوَةُ في الحُكْمِ، وهو قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ.

والثّالِثُ: هو الِاسْتِعْجالُ في القَضِيَّةِ، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ.

والرّابِعُ: ما فِيهِ الغارُّ مِنَ الأثْمانِ المُحَرَّمَةِ: كَثَمَنِ الكَلْبِ، والخِنْزِيرِ، والخَمْرِ وعَسَبِ الفَحْلِ، وحُلْوانِ الكاهِنِ.

وَأصْلُ السُّحْتِ الِاسْتِئْصالُ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَيُسْحِتَكم بِعَذابٍ﴾ أيْ يَسْتَأْصِلُكم، وقالَ الفَرَزْدَقُ:

وعَضُّ زَمانٍ يا ابْنَ مَرْوانَ لَمْ يَدَعْ مِنَ المالِ إلّا مُسْحِتًا أوْ مُجْلِفْ

فَسُمِّيَ سُحْتًا لِأنَّهُ يَسْحَتُ الدِّينَ والمُرُوءَةَ.

﴿فَإنْ جاءُوكَ فاحْكم بَيْنَهم أوْ أعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ فِيمَن أُرِيدَ بِذَلِكَ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اليَهُودِيّانِ اللَّذانِ زَنَيا، خُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُما بِالرَّجْمِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، والزُّهْرِيِّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّها في نَفْسَيْنِ مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وبَنِي النَّضِيرِ قَتَلَ أحَدُهُما صاحِبَهُ، فَخُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ عِنْدَ احْتِكامِهِما إلَيْهِ بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بِالقَوَدِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

(p-41) واخْتَلَفُوا في التَّخْيِيرِ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَهم، هَلْ هو ثابِتٌ أوْ مَنسُوخٌ؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ ثابِتٌ، وأنَّ كُلَّ حاكِمٍ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ مُخَيَّرٌ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَ أهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ (أهْلِ العَهْدِ مِن غَيْرِ المُسْلِمِينَ في دارِ الإسْلامِ) بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ، وقَتادَةَ، وعَطاءٍ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ مَنسُوخٌ (أي بالنسخ: رفع الحكم بدليل متأخر)، وأنَّ الحُكْمَ بَيْنَهم واجِبٌ عَلى مَن تَحاكَمُوا إلَيْهِ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وعُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ العَزِيزِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، وقَدْ نَسَخَهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنِ احْكم بَيْنَهم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ فِيها حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالرَّجْمِ.

والثّانِي: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالقَوَدِ.

﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: بَعْدَ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ في التَّوْراةِ.

والثّانِي: بَعْدَ تَحْكِيمِكَ.

﴿وَما أُولَئِكَ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أيْ في تَحْكِيمِكَ، أنَّهُ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ، مَعَ جُحُودِهِمْ نُبُوَّتَكَ.

والثّانِي: يَعْنِي في تَوَلِّيهِمْ عَنْ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ غَيْرَ راضِينَ بِهِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنّا أنْزَلْنا التَّوْراةَ فِيها هُدًى ونُورٌ﴾ يَعْنِي بِالهُدى الدَّلِيلُ.

وَبِالنُّورِ البَيانُ.

﴿يَحْكُمُ بِها النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أسْلَمُوا﴾ فِيهِمْ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم جَماعَةُ أنْبِياءَ مِنهم مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ. والثّانِي: المُرادُ نَبِيُّنا مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ وحْدَهُ وإنْ ذُكِرَ بِلَفْظِ الجَمْعِ.

(p-42) وَفِي الَّذِي يَحْكُمُ بِهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أرادَ رَجْمَ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ، والقَوَدَ مِنَ القاتِلِ العامِدِ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّهُ الحُكْمُ بِجَمِيعِ ما فِيها مِن غَيْرِ تَخْصِيصٍ، ما لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَسْخٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى الَّذِينَ هادُوا، وهُمُ اليَهُودُ، وفي جَوازِ الحُكْمِ بِها عَلى غَيْرِ اليَهُودِ وجْهانِ، عَلى اخْتِلافِهِمْ في التِزامِنا شَرائِعَ مَن قَبْلَنا إذا لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَصٌّ يَنْسَخُ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿والرَّبّانِيُّونَ والأحْبارُ﴾ واحِدُ الأحْبارِ حَبْرٌ بِالفَتْحِ، قالَ الفَرّاءُ: أكْثَرُ ما سَمِعْتُ حِبْرٌ بِالكَسْرِ، وهو العالِمُ، سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ اشْتِقاقًا مِنَ التَّحْبِيرِ، وهو التَّحْسِينُ، لِأنَّ العالِمَ يُحَسِّنُ الحَسَنَ ويُقَبِّحُ القَبِيحَ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ لِأنَّ العِلْمَ في نَفْسِهِ حَسَنٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ يَحْكُمُونَ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ والعُلَماءُ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

وَفي ﴿اسْتُحْفِظُوا﴾ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اسْتُودِعُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الأخْفَشِ.

والثّانِي: العِلْمُ بِما حَفِظُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الكَلْبِيِّ.

﴿وَكانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَداءَ﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى حُكْمِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أنَّهُ في التَّوْراةِ.

﴿فَلا تَخْشَوُا النّاسَ واخْشَوْنِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: فَلا تَخْشَوْهم في كِتْمانِ ما أنْزَلْتُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

والثّانِي: في الحُكْمِ بِما أنْزَلْتُ.

﴿وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِآياتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا﴾ فِيهِ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى كِتْمانِها أجْرًا.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى تَعْلِيمِها أجْرًا.

(p-43) ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكافِرُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾. وفي اخْتِلافِ هَذِهِ الآيِ الثَّلاثِ أرْبَعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّها وارِدَةٌ في اليَهُودِ دُونَ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وحُذَيْفَةَ، والبَراءِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ.

الثّانِي: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في أهْلِ الكِتابِ، وحُكْمُها عامٌّ في جَمِيعِ النّاسِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ أرادَ بِالكافِرِينَ أهْلَ الإسْلامِ، وبِالظّالِمِينَ اليَهُودَ، وبِالفاسِقِينَ النَّصارى، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّ مَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ جاحِدًا بِهِ، فَهو كافِرٌ، ومَن لَمْ يَحْكم مُقِرًّا بِهِ فَهو ظالِمٌ فاسِقٌ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الرَّسُولُ لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ في الكُفْرِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنّا بِأفْواهِهِمْ ولَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي بِهِ المُنافِقِينَ المُظْهِرِينَ لِلْإيمانِ المُبْطِنِينَ لِلْكُفْرِ.

﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي اليَهُودَ.

﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ لِيَكْذِبُوا عَلَيْكَ عِنْدَهم إذا أتَوْا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، والزَّجّاجِ.

(p-39) والثّانِي: أنَّ مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ أيْ قائِلُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ عَلَيْكَ.

وَ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ يَعْنِي في قِصَّةِ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ مِنَ اليَهُودِ الَّذِي حَكَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَأنْكَرُوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ مِن بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم إذا سَمِعُوا كَلامَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ غَيَّرُوهُ بِالكَذِبِ عَلَيْهِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: هو تَغْيِيرُ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ تَعالى في جَلْدِ الزّانِي بَدَلًا مِن رَجْمِهِ، وقِيلَ في إسْقاطِ القَوَدِ (القِصاصِ) عِنْدَ اسْتِحْقاقِهِ.

﴿يَقُولُونَ إنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذا فَخُذُوهُ وإنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فاحْذَرُوا﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: «أنَّهُ يُرِيدُ بِذَلِكَ حِينَ زَنى رَجُلٌ مِنهم بِامْرَأةٍ فَأنْفَذُوهُ إلى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهم وقالُوا: إنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالجَلْدِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ حَكَمَ عَلَيْكم بِالرَّجْمِ فَلا تَقْبَلُوهُ، فَقامَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إلى مَدارِسِ تَوْراتِهِمْ وفِيها أحْبارُهم يَتْلُونَ التَّوْراةَ، فَأتى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ صُورِيّا، وكانَ أعْوَرَ، وهو مِن أعْلَمِهِمْ فَقالَ لَهُ أسْألُكَ بِالَّذِي أنْزَلَ التَّوْراةَ بِطُورِ سَيْناءَ عَلى مُوسى بْنِ عِمْرانَ هَلْ في التَّوْراةِ الرَّجْمُ؟ فَأمْسَكَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلْ بِهِ حَتّى اعْتَرَفَ، فَأمَرَ بِهِما النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فَرُجِما، قالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: وكُنْتُ فِيمَن رَجَمَهُ وأنَّهُ لَيَقِيها الأحْجارَ بِنَفْسِهِ حَتّى ماتَتْ»، ثُمَّ إنَّ ابْنَ صُورِيّا أنْكَرَ وفِيهِ أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وجابِرٍ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ المُسَيِّبِ، والسُّدِّيِّ، وابْنِ زَيْدٍ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ في قَتِيلٍ مِنهم، قالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: قَتَلَتْ بَنُو النَّضِيرِ رَجُلًا مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وكانُوا يَمْتَنِعُونَ بِالِاسْتِطالَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ القَوَدِ بِالدِّيَةِ، وإذا قَتَلَتْ بَنُو قُرَيْظَةَ مِنهم رَجُلًا لَمْ يَقْنَعُوا إلّا بِالقَوَدِ دُونَ الدِّيَةِ، قالُوا: إنْ أفْتاكم بِالدِّيَةِ فاقْبَلُوهُ وإنْ أفْتاكم بِالقَوَدِ فَرُدُّوهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

﴿وَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُها: عَذابُهُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: إضْلالُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

(p-40) والثّالِثُ: فَضِيحَتُهُ، وهو قَوْلُ الزَّجّاجِ.

﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الضِّيقِ والحَرَجِ عُقُوبَةً لَهم.

والثّانِي: لَمْ يُطَهِّرْها مِنَ الكُفْرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أكّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾ فِيهِ أرْبَعَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ السُّحْتَ الرِّشْوَةُ، وهو مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ الرِّشْوَةُ في الحُكْمِ، وهو قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ.

والثّالِثُ: هو الِاسْتِعْجالُ في القَضِيَّةِ، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ.

والرّابِعُ: ما فِيهِ الغارُّ مِنَ الأثْمانِ المُحَرَّمَةِ: كَثَمَنِ الكَلْبِ، والخِنْزِيرِ، والخَمْرِ وعَسَبِ الفَحْلِ، وحُلْوانِ الكاهِنِ.

وَأصْلُ السُّحْتِ الِاسْتِئْصالُ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَيُسْحِتَكم بِعَذابٍ﴾ أيْ يَسْتَأْصِلُكم، وقالَ الفَرَزْدَقُ:

وعَضُّ زَمانٍ يا ابْنَ مَرْوانَ لَمْ يَدَعْ مِنَ المالِ إلّا مُسْحِتًا أوْ مُجْلِفْ

فَسُمِّيَ سُحْتًا لِأنَّهُ يَسْحَتُ الدِّينَ والمُرُوءَةَ.

﴿فَإنْ جاءُوكَ فاحْكم بَيْنَهم أوْ أعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ فِيمَن أُرِيدَ بِذَلِكَ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اليَهُودِيّانِ اللَّذانِ زَنَيا، خُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُما بِالرَّجْمِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، والزُّهْرِيِّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّها في نَفْسَيْنِ مِن بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ وبَنِي النَّضِيرِ قَتَلَ أحَدُهُما صاحِبَهُ، فَخُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ عِنْدَ احْتِكامِهِما إلَيْهِ بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ بِالقَوَدِ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

(p-41) واخْتَلَفُوا في التَّخْيِيرِ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَهم، هَلْ هو ثابِتٌ أوْ مَنسُوخٌ؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ ثابِتٌ، وأنَّ كُلَّ حاكِمٍ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ مُخَيَّرٌ في الحُكْمِ بَيْنَ أهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ (أهْلِ العَهْدِ مِن غَيْرِ المُسْلِمِينَ في دارِ الإسْلامِ) بَيْنَ أنْ يَحْكُمَ أوْ يَدَعَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ، وقَتادَةَ، وعَطاءٍ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ذَلِكَ مَنسُوخٌ (أي بالنسخ: رفع الحكم بدليل متأخر)، وأنَّ الحُكْمَ بَيْنَهم واجِبٌ عَلى مَن تَحاكَمُوا إلَيْهِ مِن حُكّامِ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وعُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ العَزِيزِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، وقَدْ نَسَخَهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنِ احْكم بَيْنَهم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ فِيها حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالرَّجْمِ.

والثّانِي: حُكْمُ اللَّهِ بِالقَوَدِ.

﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: بَعْدَ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ في التَّوْراةِ.

والثّانِي: بَعْدَ تَحْكِيمِكَ.

﴿وَما أُولَئِكَ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أيْ في تَحْكِيمِكَ، أنَّهُ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ، مَعَ جُحُودِهِمْ نُبُوَّتَكَ.

والثّانِي: يَعْنِي في تَوَلِّيهِمْ عَنْ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ غَيْرَ راضِينَ بِهِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنّا أنْزَلْنا التَّوْراةَ فِيها هُدًى ونُورٌ﴾ يَعْنِي بِالهُدى الدَّلِيلُ.

وَبِالنُّورِ البَيانُ.

﴿يَحْكُمُ بِها النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أسْلَمُوا﴾ فِيهِمْ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم جَماعَةُ أنْبِياءَ مِنهم مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ. والثّانِي: المُرادُ نَبِيُّنا مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ وحْدَهُ وإنْ ذُكِرَ بِلَفْظِ الجَمْعِ.

(p-42) وَفِي الَّذِي يَحْكُمُ بِهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ أرادَ رَجْمَ الزّانِي المُحْصَنِ، والقَوَدَ مِنَ القاتِلِ العامِدِ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّهُ الحُكْمُ بِجَمِيعِ ما فِيها مِن غَيْرِ تَخْصِيصٍ، ما لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَسْخٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى الَّذِينَ هادُوا، وهُمُ اليَهُودُ، وفي جَوازِ الحُكْمِ بِها عَلى غَيْرِ اليَهُودِ وجْهانِ، عَلى اخْتِلافِهِمْ في التِزامِنا شَرائِعَ مَن قَبْلَنا إذا لَمْ يَرِدْ بِهِ نَصٌّ يَنْسَخُ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿والرَّبّانِيُّونَ والأحْبارُ﴾ واحِدُ الأحْبارِ حَبْرٌ بِالفَتْحِ، قالَ الفَرّاءُ: أكْثَرُ ما سَمِعْتُ حِبْرٌ بِالكَسْرِ، وهو العالِمُ، سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ اشْتِقاقًا مِنَ التَّحْبِيرِ، وهو التَّحْسِينُ، لِأنَّ العالِمَ يُحَسِّنُ الحَسَنَ ويُقَبِّحُ القَبِيحَ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ لِأنَّ العِلْمَ في نَفْسِهِ حَسَنٌ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ يَحْكُمُونَ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ والعُلَماءُ بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ.

وَفي ﴿اسْتُحْفِظُوا﴾ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: اسْتُودِعُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الأخْفَشِ.

والثّانِي: العِلْمُ بِما حَفِظُوا، وهو قَوْلُ الكَلْبِيِّ.

﴿وَكانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَداءَ﴾ يَعْنِي عَلى حُكْمِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أنَّهُ في التَّوْراةِ.

﴿فَلا تَخْشَوُا النّاسَ واخْشَوْنِ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: فَلا تَخْشَوْهم في كِتْمانِ ما أنْزَلْتُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

والثّانِي: في الحُكْمِ بِما أنْزَلْتُ.

﴿وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِآياتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا﴾ فِيهِ تَأْوِيلانِ: أحَدُهُما: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى كِتْمانِها أجْرًا.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ لا تَأْخُذُوا عَلى تَعْلِيمِها أجْرًا.

(p-43) ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكافِرُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾، ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾. وفي اخْتِلافِ هَذِهِ الآيِ الثَّلاثِ أرْبَعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّها وارِدَةٌ في اليَهُودِ دُونَ المُسْلِمِينَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وحُذَيْفَةَ، والبَراءِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ.

الثّانِي: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في أهْلِ الكِتابِ، وحُكْمُها عامٌّ في جَمِيعِ النّاسِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ أرادَ بِالكافِرِينَ أهْلَ الإسْلامِ، وبِالظّالِمِينَ اليَهُودَ، وبِالفاسِقِينَ النَّصارى، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّ مَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ جاحِدًا بِهِ، فَهو كافِرٌ، ومَن لَمْ يَحْكم مُقِرًّا بِهِ فَهو ظالِمٌ فاسِقٌ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verses 45–47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that a life is for a life﴾ — the verse.

It was revealed concerning the Jews of the Banu Qurayza and the Nadir, and we have already mentioned their story.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him.﴾ On this there are two opinions. The first: it is an expiation for the wounds (of the victim), and this is the view of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, Ibrahim (al-Nakhaʿi), al-Hasan (al-Basri), and al-Shaʿbi. Al-Shaʿbi narrated from Ibn al-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is wounded in his body and forgives it, Allah will expiate his sins to the same extent that he forgave." The second: it is an expiation for the one who inflicted the wound (the offender), because it takes the place of exacting the right from him. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid. This is to be understood as applying to the one who was pardoned after his repentance.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verses 48–50:

Allah's words: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

﴿Confirming what was before it of the Book﴾, meaning confirming what came before it of the Scripture. In this there are two interpretations. First: confirming them (the earlier books), and this is the view of Muqatil. Second: agreeing with them, and this is the view of al-Kalbi.

﴿And a guardian over it﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations. The first: meaning trustworthy (amin), and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas. The second: meaning a witness over it, and this is the view of Qatadah and al-Suddi. The third: meaning a protector over it (hafiz 'alayhi).

﴿So judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾. This indicates the obligation to judge between the People of the Book when they bring their disputes to us, and that we should not judge between them by their Torah or their Gospel.

﴿And do not follow their desires, away from the truth that has come to you. For each of you We have made﴾. Concerning "them" (in "for each of you") there are two views. The first: they are the community of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). The second: they are the communities of all the Prophets.

﴿A law and a way﴾. As for shir'ah (law), it is the sharia, which is the clear path, and whatever you prescribe (shara'ta) in anything is a shari'ah. From this it is said that the shari'ah of water (the place to reach water) is called shari'ah, because it is the most apparent of its routes to it. From this is also the saying of the Arabs: "ushri'at al-asinnah" (the spear-points were made to appear) when they became visible.

As for minhaj, it is the clear road. It is said: "tariq nahj" and "manhaj" (a clear road). The poet al-Zajir said:

"Whoever is in doubt, here is the clear spring of water, fresh and quenching, and a clear road."

So the meaning of His words "a law and a way" is: a path and a sunnah. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatadah.

﴿And had Allah willed, He would have made you one community﴾. Concerning this there are two views. The first: to make you upon one religion (millah). The second: to gather you upon the truth, and this is the view of al-Hasan.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verses 54–56:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him﴾. There are three opinions concerning them:

The first: they are Abu Bakr and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, who fought alongside him against the people of apostasy (ahl al-ridda). This was said by ʿAli, al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Dahhak.

The second: they are the people of Abu Musa al-Ashari from the people of Yemen, because they had a good effect in supporting Islam. It has been narrated that "when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) gestured toward Abu Musa al-Ashari with something that was in his hand and said: (They are the people of this man)." This was said by Mujahid and Shurayh.

﴿Humble toward the believers﴾: meaning, tender and merciful toward them.

﴿Mighty toward the disbelievers﴾: meaning, harsh and stern toward them. This is related from ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas.

In the recitation of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud it is: "humble toward the believers, harsh (ghuluzun) toward the disbelievers."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed﴾ — the verse. Concerning this verse there are two opinions:

One: it was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and those who embraced Islam with him from among his companions, when they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the hostility the Jews displayed toward them. This was said by al-Kalbi.

(p-49) The second: it was revealed concerning ʿUbada ibn al-Samit when he disavowed the alliance with the Jews and said: "I take Allah and His Messenger as my guardians."

Concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who establish prayer and give zakat while they are bowing [in ruku]﴾, there are two opinions:

One: it refers to ʿAli, who gave charity while he was in ruku. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: it is general, encompassing all believers. This was said by al-Hasan and al-Suddi.

Concerning His saying: ﴿while they are bowing﴾, there are three aspects:

The first: they did this during their ruku.

The second: it was revealed concerning them while they were in their ruku.

The third: by ruku he meant voluntary prayer (al-tanafful), and by establishing prayer he meant the obligatory prayer (al-fard), from the expression "so-and-so bows (yarka'u)" when he performs voluntary prayer.

The rabbaniyyun are the scholars of the Gospel (al-Injil), and the ahbar are the scholars of the Torah (al-Tawrah).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verse 64–66:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Hand of Allah is chained up."﴾ Regarding this there are two interpretations. The first: meaning it is withheld from giving, out of miserliness. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah.

The second: meaning it is withheld from punishing them. This was said by al-Hasan.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: the one who said this was Phinehas (Finhas) and his companions from the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa.

﴿Their hands are chained up﴾: regarding this there are two views. The first: he said this as a rebuke to them for miserliness, in keeping with the correspondence of the speech (ʿala mutabaqat al-kalam), as said by al-Zajjaj.

The second: its meaning is that their hands will literally be chained up in Hell. This was said by al-Hasan.

﴿And they are cursed for what they said.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: that is, He punishes them with the jizya (poll tax).

It is also possible that their cursing is their expulsion when they were exiled from their homes.

﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾: regarding this there are four interpretations. Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verse 67:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. By this verse Allah, exalted is He, made it obligatory upon His Messenger to convey what was sent down to him of His Book, whether it was a ruling (hukm), a hadd (fixed punishment), or retaliation (qisas). As for conveying other revelation, its obligation is restricted to what pertains to the rulings (ahkam) and not to other matters.

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾. It means: if you conceal a single verse of what was sent down to you, then you have not conveyed His message, because you would not be complying with the whole command.

It may bear two other meanings.

The first: its meaning is, "Convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord concerning the promise of victory He has made to you. If you do not, then you have not conveyed the true substance of His message concerning the command He has imposed on you, because the sense of being assured of victory moves one to comply with the command."

The second: its meaning is, "Convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord in a manner that obliges submission to it through striving (jihad) for it. If you do not do what leads to striving for it, then you have not conveyed to them what is due to you of the right of the message."

﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾: that is, that they should harm you with any evil, whether by killing or otherwise.

The exegetes differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this, on two accounts. The first: "The Prophet ﷺ halted at a place on his journey and sheltered beneath a tree, resting under it at midday. A Bedouin came to him, drew his sword, and said: 'Who will protect you from me?' He said: 'Allah.' The Bedouin's hand trembled, his sword fell, and he struck his head against the tree until his brains spilled out. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾." This was related by Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi.

The second: "The Prophet ﷺ used to fear Quraysh, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse." This was related by Ibn Jurayj.

And 'A'isha narrated: "The Prophet ﷺ used to be guarded until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. Then the Prophet ﷺ put his head out of the tent and said: 'O people, disperse, for Allah has protected me.'"

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾: concerning this there are two interpretations. The first: He does not help them to attain their aim. The second: He does not guide them to Paradise.

**Al-Mawardi's commentary:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾. There are two interpretations of this. The first is that the covenant consists of clear signs, which the knowledge they possess confirms.

The second is that the covenant consists of oaths which the prophets of the Children of Israel took from them, that they would act upon them, and that they were commanded to affirm His messengers.

﴿And We sent to them messengers﴾, meaning after the taking of the covenant.

﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire﴾. Hawa al-nafs (the desire of the soul) is written with a short alif (hawā, *hawa*), while hawa al-jaww (the air of the atmosphere) is written with a long alif (hawāʾ, *hawaa'*). Both share the meaning of the word, because the soul takes pleasure in its desire just as it takes pleasure in the air of the atmosphere.

﴿A party they called liars, and a party they killed﴾. This means that when the prophets did not permit them what they desired in the religion, they denied a party of them, and they killed a party. They had denied those whom they killed, but the sense of the sentence is that they limited themselves to denying one party and went beyond that to killing another party.

﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾. There are three interpretations of it. The first: it is the punishment that descends from the sky. The second: what they were tested with, namely the killing of the prophets and their denial. The third: what they were afflicted with at the hands of the disbelievers who overpowered them.

﴿So they became blind and deaf﴾. This means they became blind to the guide and deaf to the admonition, to the point that they hastened to kill their prophets when they thought there would be no trial.

﴿Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness﴾. This means that they repented after witnessing the trial, so Allah accepted their repentance.

﴿Then they became blind and deaf again﴾. This means that after repentance they returned to what they had been upon before it. The return was only from most of them, not from all of them. (p-56)

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verse 72–75:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger﴾. By this God refuted the Jews and the Christians. He refuted the Jews in their denial of his prophethood and their attributing him to other than a legitimate lineage, and He refuted the Christians in their saying that he is the son of God.

﴿And his mother was a truthful woman﴾. He refuted the Jews in their attributing her to immorality.

Regarding His saying ﴿truthful (siddiqah)﴾, there are two interpretations. One is that it is an intensification of her truthfulness and of the negation of immorality from her.

The second is that she believed in the signs of her Lord, and so she was in the position of her son. This is the view of al-Hasan.

﴿They both used to eat food﴾. Concerning this there are two views. One is that by it He alluded to defecation, since it issues from them, and this is a attribute that is negated of God.

The second is that He meant eating itself, because need for it is a deficiency, and God is not deficient.

﴿Look how We make the signs clear to them﴾, meaning the proofs and evidences.

(p-57) ﴿Then look how they are turned away﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations. The first: they are turned away (yusrafun), from their saying "the land was turned away (ufikat)" when rain was diverted from it.

The second: they are turned over (yuqlabun), and the "mu'tafikat" are the things overturned by winds and other things.

The third: they lie (yakdhibun), from ifk, which is falsehood.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verses 76–86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with Allah﴾, meaning the idol-worshippers among the Arabs. The two groups united in enmity against the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians."﴾ This is not general; it is specific. Regarding it there are two opinions. The first: it refers to the Negus (al-Najashi) and his companions when they embraced Islam. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

The second: they are a people from among the Christians who were upon the truth, adhering to the law of ʿIsa (peace be upon him). When Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, they believed in him. This was said by Qatadah.

﴿That is because among them are qissisin (priests) and ruhban (monks)﴾. The singular of qissisin is qass, derived from qassa, and they are the worshippers.

The singular of ruhban is rahib, and they are the ascetics.

﴿And that they are not arrogant﴾, meaning, toward submitting to the truth when it binds them, and toward the proof when it is established.

(p-59) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations.

The first: it refers to the seizure of wealth that is pleasant and good, so that by being taken through usurpation it becomes unlawful, although they could have reached it by a lawful means. This was said by some of the Basrans.

The second: it refers to the prohibition of the good things that had been permitted to them. The cause of this was that a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), among them ʿAlī, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, Ibn Masʿūd, and Ibn ʿUmar, resolved to fast perpetually, to stand in prayer through the night, to abstain from women, to castrate themselves, and to forbid themselves the good foods. So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed concerning them: ﴿Do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾, and ﴿Do not transgress; indeed Allah does not love the transgressors﴾. Regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first: do not transgress by usurping wealth that is forbidden to you.

The second: by transgression is meant what ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn resolved upon, namely castrating himself; this was said by al-Suddī.

The third: it refers to what the group had resolved upon concerning the prohibition of women, food, clothing, and sleep; this was said by ʿIkrimah.

The fourth: it is going beyond the lawful to the unlawful; this was said by al-Ḥasan.

(p-60) The Exalted said: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintended in your oaths﴾. We have already mentioned the disagreement of the exegetes (mufassirun) and jurists (fuqaha') regarding the idle oath (lagh al-yamin, an oath sworn without intention to bind oneself).

﴿But He holds you accountable for the oaths you have deliberately sworn﴾. There is disagreement about the occasion of its revelation, on two views:

(p-60) The first: "It was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Maz'un, when he forbade himself food and women by an oath he had sworn, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to break it." This was related by al-Suddi.

The second: "It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Rawahah. He had a guest, but his wife delayed serving his hospitality, so he swore he would not eat any food. The wife swore she would not eat it if he did not eat, and the guest swore he would not eat it if they did not eat. So Abdullah ate, and they ate with him. The Prophet ﷺ was informed of this and said: 'You did well,' and this verse was revealed concerning it." This was related by Ibn Zayd.

The Exalted's words: ﴿But He holds you accountable for the oaths you have deliberately sworn﴾. Their binding (aqd) is a verbal utterance with the tongue together with an intention in the heart, because whatever one did not intend in one's oaths is idle, and one is not held accountable for it.

Then, regarding their binding, there are two views. The first: that it be upon a future action, and not upon a past report. A future action is of two kinds: negation and affirmation. Negation is to say, "By Allah, I will not do such-and-such." Affirmation is to say, "By Allah, I will certainly do such-and-such."

As for a past report, it is to say, "By Allah, I did not do it," when he did it, or to say, "By Allah, I did do such-and-such," when he did not. His oath is binding by a future action in both its affirmative and negative forms.

There are two views on whether an oath is binding by a past report.

The first: it is not binding by a past report. This was said by Abu Hanifah and the people of Iraq (Ahl al-Iraq).

The second view: it is binding upon a future action and upon a past report, in both of which breaking (hint, violating the oath) applies. This was said by al-Shafi'i and the people of the Hijaz (Ahl al-Hijaz).

Then the Exalted said: ﴿So its expiation (kaffarah, atonement) is feeding ten needy persons﴾. Regarding this there are two views. The first: it is the expiation of the oaths they bound themselves by. This was said by Aisha, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and Qatadah.

The second: it is the expiation of breaking the oath they bound themselves by. This appears to be the view of Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and Ibrahim.

(p-60) The most correct way of applying these two views is to consider the state of the oath in its binding and its breaking, for it is never free of three conditions. The first: its binding and its breaking are both sinful, such as saying, "By Allah, I will not kill a soul or drink wine." If he breaks it, kills a soul, and drinks wine, the expiation is to atone for the sin of breaking it.

The third condition: its binding is permissible and its breaking is permissible, such as saying, "By Allah, I will not wear this garment." The expiation is attached to both, though it is more specifically tied to breaking.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾. Regarding this there are two views. The first: from the average of the kinds of food. This was said by Ibn Umar, al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin.

The second: from the average in quantity. This was said by Ali, Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited (min wasat ma tut'imuna ahlikum), with wasat instead of awsat. Then they differed about the quantity, on five sayings:

The first: it is one mudd (a measure of about a handful and a half to two handfuls, roughly 500–700 g) of the various kinds of food. This was said by Ibn Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ata', and Qatadah, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i.

The second: it is half a sa' (a measure of about two and a half to three kilograms) of the various kinds of food. This was said by Ali and Umar, and it is the position of Abu Hanifah.

The third: it is lunch and dinner. This was said by Ali in the narration of al-Harith from him, and it is the view of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Hasan al-Basri.

The fourth: it is what the one making expiation customarily gives his dependents. If he fills them, he fills the needy; if he does not fill them, it is according to that measure. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The fifth: it is one of two things, either lunch or dinner. This was said by some of the Basrans (al-Basriyyun).

Then the Exalted said: ﴿or clothing them﴾. There are five views regarding this. The first: the clothing of one garment. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Tawus, Ata', and al-Shafi'i.

(p-62) The second: the clothing of two garments. This was said by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin.

The third: the clothing of one comprehensive garment, such as a wrap or a cloak. This was said by Ibrahim.

The fourth: the clothing of a waist-wrap, a shawl, and a shirt. This was said by Ibn Umar.

The fifth: the clothing with which prayer is valid. This was said by some of the Basrans.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿or freeing a slave﴾, meaning: or releasing a neck from the captivity of bondage to the state of freedom and liberation. Fakk (release) means manumission. Al-Farazdaq said:

"O Banu Ghadanah, indeed I freed you,
then I gave you to Atiyyah ibn Ja'al."

It is valid for the slave to be young or old, male or female. Regarding the entitlement to their price there are two views. The first: it is owed (to the slave's master), and the expiation is not valid with him. This was said by al-Shafi'i.

The second: it is not owed. This was said by Abu Hanifah.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever cannot find [it], then fasting three days﴾. Allah made fasting a substitute for wealth when one is unable to provide it, and when one is well-off He made one free to choose between expiation by feeding, by clothing, or by manumission. Regarding this there are two views. The first: that what is obligatory from among these is one of them, which he does not specify, according to the majority of jurists.

The second: that all of them are obligatory, and he may suffice with one of them. This was said by some theologians (mutakallimun), and it is an anomalous view among the jurists.

This is a difference in wording only, not in meaning, when examined.

There is disagreement about the case where one does not find (the means) and fasts, on five views. The first: if he does not find his staple food and the staple food of those he supports, he fasts. This was said by al-Shafi'i.

The second: if he does not find three dirhams, he fasts. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The third: if he does not find two dirhams, he fasts. This was said by al-Hasan.

(p-63) The fourth: if he does not find two hundred dirhams, he fasts. This was said by Abu Hanifah.

The fifth: if he does not find anything beyond his capital with which he trades for his livelihood, he fasts.

Regarding the consecutiveness of this fasting, there are two views. The first: it is obligatory. This was said by Mujahid and Ibrahim, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to recite: (fasting three days, consecutive) (fa-siyam thalathat ayyam mutatabi'at). The second: if he fasts them separated, it is permissible. This was said by Malik, and by al-Shafi'i in one of his two views.

﴿That is the expiation of your oaths when you swear﴾, meaning: and break them. If it is asked, "Why did He not mention repentance together with the expiation?" It is answered: because not every oath that is broken is a sin that requires repentance. If sin accompanies it, repentance becomes obligatory through regret and abandoning the resolve to return to it.

(p. 66) The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with some of the game﴾. Regarding His words "will surely test you," there are two interpretations. The first: its meaning is "will impose obligations upon you." The second: "will try you," as said by Qutrub and al-Kalbi.

Regarding His words ﴿some of the game﴾, there are two views. The first: *min* (مِنَ, "of/some") is partitive (lil-tab'id) in this place, because the ruling applies to the game of the land and not the sea, and to the game of the sacred precinct (haram) and the state of ihram (ritual consecration) and not to the game outside the sacred precinct or outside ihram. The second: *min* in this place is explicative (li-bayan al-jins), as in His words: ﴿So avoid the abomination, which is of idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30], as said by al-Zajjaj.

﴿Which your hands and your spears can reach﴾: regarding this there are two interpretations. The first: "what our hands can reach" means the eggs (of birds), and "our spears" means the game (larger animals), as said by Mujahid. The second: "what our hands can reach" means the young, and "our spears" means the grown, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

﴿That Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen﴾: regarding this there are four interpretations. The first: the meaning of "that Allah may know" is "that He may see," and knowledge is expressed here by what leads to it, as said by al-Kalbi. The second: "that His friends may know who fears Him in the unseen." The third: "that you may know that Allah knows who fears Him in the unseen." The fourth: its meaning is "that you may fear Allah in the unseen," and "knowing" is metaphorical; His words "in the unseen" mean "in secret, as you fear Him openly."

﴿Whoever transgresses after that﴾ means whoever transgresses in hunting after the prohibition has been revealed.

﴿For him there is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., painful. Al-Kalbi said: it was revealed on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, when people were surrounded by game while they were in ihram.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in ihram (ḥurum)﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations. The first: it means being in ihram for hajj or 'umrah, as said by most scholars. The second: "ḥurum" means one who has entered the sacred precinct (haram). It is said: *aḥrama* when one enters the haram, *atham* when one enters Tihamah, and *anjada* when one enters Najd; and it is said *aḥrama* of one who enters the sacred months. This was said by some of the Basran scholars. The third: the term "muḥrim" (one in ihram) applies to both meanings together in its literal sense, not metaphorically, to one who enters ihram for hajj or 'umrah or enters the haram; and the ruling on killing game in both cases is equal by the apparent meaning of the verse, as said by Ali ibn Abi Hurayra.

﴿And whoever of you kills it intentionally﴾: regarding this there are two views. The first: intentionally killing it while forgetting that he is in ihram, as said by Mujahid, Ibrahim and Ibn Jurayj. The second: intentionally killing it while remembering that he is in ihram, as said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata' and al-Zuhri.

They differed concerning one who kills by mistake, forgetting that he is in ihram, on two views. The first: there is no compensation (jaza') for him, as said by Dawud. The second: he owes compensation, as said by Malik, al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifah.

﴿Then the compensation is like what he killed of livestock﴾, i.e., the compensation for killing in the haram or in ihram is like what he killed of livestock (al-na'am).

Regarding "like" (mithl) there are two views. The first: the value of the game is spent on something like it from livestock, as said by Abu Hanifah. The second: he owes an animal of livestock similar to the game in form and resemblance, as said by al-Shafi'i.

﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾, i.e., regarding the like from livestock. Thus the equivalent is not determined except by the judgment of two just jurists, and it is permissible for the killer to be one of them.

﴿As an offering (hady) reaching the Ka'bah﴾: he means that the equivalent of the game from livestock must be delivered to the Ka'bah, and by "the Ka'bah" he means the entire haram, because it is within the haram.

They differed as to whether it is permissible to offer in the sacred state (ḥurum) what is not permissible in the sacrifice (udhiyah), such as young sheep, on two views. The first: it is not permissible, as said by Abu Hanifah. The second: it is permissible, as said by al-Shafi'i.

﴿Or expiation (kaffarah) is feeding the needy﴾: regarding this there are two views. (p. 68) The first: he estimates the equivalent from livestock and buys food with its value, as said by 'Ata' and al-Shafi'i. The second: he estimates the game and buys food with the value, as said by Qatadah and Abu Hanifah.

﴿Or its equivalent in fasting﴾, i.e., the equivalent of the food in fasting. Regarding this there are three sayings. The first: he fasts one day for each *mudd* (a measure of about a handful or less, roughly a quarter of a *sa'*), as said by 'Ata' and al-Shafi'i. The second: he fasts three days for each *mudd*, as said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The third: he fasts two days for each *sa'*, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

They differed concerning expiation by these three options, whether it is in sequence (tartib) or by choice (takhyir), on two views. The first: it is in sequence; if he does not find the equivalent, then feeding; if he cannot find food, then fasting. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Amir, Ibrahim and al-Suddi. The second: it is by choice, that he expiates by whichever of the three he wishes. This was said by 'Ata', and it is one of the two views of Ibn 'Abbas, and the position of al-Shafi'i.

﴿That he may taste the consequence of his affair﴾, i.e., in undertaking the expiation and the obligation of repentance.

﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾, i.e., before the revelation of the prohibition.

﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾: regarding this there are two views. The first: i.e., whoever returns after the prohibition, Allah will take retribution from him by the compensation in this world, and by the punishment for disobedience in the Hereafter. The second: whoever returns after the prohibition to killing game a second time after his first, Allah will take retribution from him.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verse 96–99:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea﴾, meaning the game of the water, whether it comes from a sea, a river, a spring or a well. Its game is lawful for the one in ihram and for the one not in ihram, both within the sacred precincts and outside them.

﴿and its food is a provision for you and for the travellers﴾. Regarding its "food" there are two opinions. The first: it is what floats on it and what the sea casts up. This was said by Abu Bakr, Umar and Qatadah.

The second: it is what has been salted. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verses 100–102:

Allah's words: ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal⦘ — there are three interpretations concerning it. The first: it means the lawful (ḥalāl) and the unlawful (ḥarām); this is the view of al-Ḥasan. The second: the believer and the disbeliever; this is the view of al-Suddī. The third: the bad (radī') and the good (jayyid).

﴿And though the abundance of the evil should please you⦘ — meaning that the lawful and the good, despite their scarcity, are better and more beneficial than the unlawful and the bad, despite their abundance.

Muqātil said: this verse was revealed concerning the pilgrims of Yamāmah, when the Muslims intended to act against one of them.

Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you⦘ — the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse, in three statements. The first: what Anas ibn Mālik narrated, who said: "The people kept asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until they pressed him hard with questions. He ascended the pulpit one day and said: (Do not ask me about anything except that I will make it clear to you).' Anas said: 'I began looking to my right and left, and I saw every person with his garment over his head, weeping. A man who used to be called to other than his father when he quarrelled asked: "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" He said: (Your father is Ḥudhāfah).' Then 'Umar stood up and said: 'We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as Messenger; I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of trials.' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you⦘." The second: what al-Ḥasan ibn Wāqid narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said: (O people, Allah has prescribed for you the Ḥajj, so perform it). Muḥṣin al-Asadī stood up and said: 'Every year, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: (If I had said yes, it would have become obligatory; and if it had become obligatory and you had abandoned it, you would have gone astray. Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets).' Then Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask⦘." The third: that it was revealed concerning a people who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah, the waṣīlah and the ḥām; this is the view of Ibn 'Abbās.

﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you⦘ — he made the descent of the Qur'an at the time of questioning a cause for the answer being hastened.

﴿Allah has pardoned you for them⦘ — concerning this there are two statements. One: "for the asking of them." The second: "for the things about which they asked."

Allah's words: ﴿A people before you asked about them, then became disbelievers because of them⦘ — concerning this there are four interpretations. The first: they are the people of 'Īsā, who asked him for the table (al-mā'idah), then disbelieved after it; this is the view of Ibn 'Abbās. The second: they are the people of Ṣāliḥ, who asked for the she-camel, then they slaughtered her and disbelieved in him. The third: they are the Quraysh, who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to turn al-Ṣafā into gold for them; this is the view of al-Suddī. The fourth: they are the people who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "Who is my father?" and the like, and when he informed them of it, they denied it and disbelieved in him; this is the view of some of the later scholars.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verse 103–104:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has not instituted any bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham﴾. Meaning: Allah did not slit the ear of any bahira, nor let loose any sa'iba, nor join any wasila, nor protect any ham.

Abu Salih narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to Aktham ibn Jawn: 'O Aktham, I saw Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'a ibn Khindif dragging his intestines in the Fire. I have never seen a man more like a man than you are like him, nor him more like you than you are.' Aktham said: 'I fear that his resemblance will harm me, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'No, you are a believer, and he is an unbeliever. He was the first to alter the religion of Isma'il, to slit the ear of the bahira, to let loose the sa'iba, and to protect the ham.'" The meaning of his saying "dragging his qusb in the Fire" is that he is dragging his intestines. The bahira is the split (fasla) from the speech of the speaker: "I slit the ear of the she-camel (bahartu udhn al-naqa)" when he splits it. From this is the saying of al-Ubayrid:

"And Imran walks among you as if he were a split-eared camel."

(p-73) Abu Ishaq narrated from Abu al-Ahwas, from his father, who said: "I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Do you see your camels, their ears intact, then you take the knife and slit them, saying "this is a bahira"? And you split their ears saying "this is a bahira"?' He said: 'Indeed, the strength of Allah is greater, and the blade of Allah is sharper; every property of yours is lawful for you, nothing of it is forbidden to you.'"

There are three opinions concerning the bahira. The first: the bahira is a she-camel that has given birth to five litters; if the fifth was a male, men would eat it to the exclusion of women; if it was a female, they would slit its ear, that is split it, and leave it, so no milk of it is drunk, it is not slaughtered, and it is not ridden; and if it died, both men and women shared in it. This is the view of Ikrima.

The second opinion: the bahira is the she-camel that bears five litters, and the last of them was a male that died; they slit the ear of the she-camel and let it go, so it is not milked nor ridden, out of scruple. This is the view of Abu Ubayda.

The third opinion: the bahira is the daughter of the sa'iba. This is the view of Abu Ishaq. As for the sa'iba, it is the musayyaba, the released one. The Arabs used to do this with some of their livestock, forbidding the benefit of them to themselves, seeking nearness to Allah, the Exalted. The poet said:

"You have hamstrung a she-camel that belonged to my Lord, and a sa'iba, so stand up for punishment."

Likewise some of the people of Islam would free their slave as a sa'iba, not benefiting from him nor from his walaʾ. Abu al-Aliya was a sa'iba; when his master was brought his inheritance, he said: "He is a sa'iba," and refused to take it.

The musayyaba was expressed by the wording of sa'iba, as it is said in "a pleasing life" (ʿīshatin rāḍiya), meaning pleasing. Regarding the sa'iba there are two opinions. The first: it is a she-camel that bears ten females in succession with no male among them; it is let loose, its back is not ridden, its wool is not shorn, and no one drinks its milk except a guest. Whatever it bears after that of a female, its ear is slit, it is called bahira, and it is left with its mother. This is the view of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

The second opinion: they used to vow the sa'iba when ill, so a man would let his camel loose (p-74) and it would not be ridden, nor would it be driven away from water, like the bahira. This is the view of Abu Ubayda.

As for the wasila, they agreed that it is from sheep, and concerning it there are three opinions. The first: it is the ewe that gives birth to seven litters; they examine the seventh litter, and if it is a male kid they slaughter it, and men eat it to the exclusion of women. They say: "This is lawful for our males, forbidden to our wives and women." If it is a female (ʿanāq), it is let loose to graze with the flock of the tribe. If it is a male and female together, they say: "It has joined its brother (waṣalat akhāhā)," so it is called wasila. This is the view of Ikrima.

The second opinion: it is the ewe that brings forth ten females in five litters with no male among them; it is made a wasila, and they say: "It has joined," and whatever it bears after that is for the males to the exclusion of the females. This is the view of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

The third opinion: when a ewe bore them a male, the Arabs would say: "This is for our gods," and draw near through it; when it bore a female, they would say: "This is for us"; and when it bore a male and female, they would say: "It has joined its brother," so they would not slaughter him on her account. This is the view of Abu Ubayda.

As for the ham, there is one opinion on which they agreed: it is the camel that produces ten litters from its loins, so it is said: "its back has been protected," and it is let go.

If it is a male and female together, they say: "It has joined its brother (waṣalat akhāhā)," so it is called wasila. This is the view of Ikrima.

The second opinion: it is the ewe that brings forth ten females in five litters with no male among them; it is made a wasila, and they say: "It has joined," and whatever it bears after that is for the males to the exclusion of the females. This is the view of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

The third opinion: when a ewe bore them a male, the Arabs would say: "This is for our gods," and draw near through it; when it bore a female, they would say: "This is for us"; and when it bore a male and female, they would say: "It has joined its brother," so they would not slaughter him on her account. This is the view of Abu Ubayda.

As for the ham, there is one opinion on which they agreed: it is the camel that produces ten litters from its loins, so it is said: "its back has been protected," and it is let go.

(p-76) ﴿and the disaster of death strikes you﴾. In the statement there is an ellipsis (mahdhuf), its implied sense being: "and the disaster of death strikes you, and you have entrusted the bequest to them both."

﴿Nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah﴾, meaning, that which He has made obligatory upon us.

His statement: ﴿And if it becomes known that the two had committed sin﴾, meaning, if it is found that they lied and betrayed, and He expressed the lie by betrayal and sin because it arose from them both.

﴿Then two others [will stand] in their place﴾, meaning from among the heirs.

﴿Among those who have the claim against them﴾, in the oath, when the betrayal became apparent.

Then the cup was found in Makkah, and they said, 'We bought it from Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi ibn Bada'.' And Allah does not guide the defiant people.﴾"

(p-78) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers and say, "What response were you given?" They will say, "We have no knowledge."﴾ Regarding His saying, ﴿We have no knowledge﴾, there are five interpretations.

First: this was not a denial of what they knew, but they were stunned and forgot the answer because of the terror of that Day; then, after their intellects had settled, they answered. This is the view of al-Hasan and al-Suddi.

Second: "We have no knowledge except what You have taught us." This is the view of Mujahid.

Third: "We have no knowledge except a knowledge You know better than we do." This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

Fourth: "We have no knowledge of what their nations answered them with, because that is what the reward is based upon." This is also narrated from al-Hasan.

Fifth: the meaning of His saying, ﴿What response were you given?﴾, is: what did they do after you (i.e., what did their nations do after you departed?). ﴿They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ This is the view of Ibn Jurayj.

Regarding His saying, ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾, there are two interpretations. The first: it is an intensive form (hyperbole). The second: it denotes one who knows a great many things (unseen matters).

If it is asked: why did He ask them about what He Himself knows better than they do? There are two answers to this. The first: He asked them in order to make them aware of what they did not know of their peoples' disbelief, hypocrisy, and their lying against them after them. The second: He intended to expose them thereby before the witnesses, so that this would be a kind of punishment for them.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 5, verses 110–111:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you"﴾. Allah reminded Jesus, peace be upon him, of His favour upon him and upon his mother, although He is the One who remembers both of them for two reasons:

First: so that He may recite to the nations the honour with which He singled him out and the elevated station with which He distinguished him.

Second: so that He may thereby confirm His proof and refute the one who denies it.

Then the Exalted began to enumerate His favours, saying: ﴿When I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit﴾. That is, "I strengthened you." It is derived from al-ayd, which means strength. The Holy Spirit is Jibril (Gabriel), and al-Quds (the Holy) is Allah, exalted be His names.

His strengthening of him has two aspects: First: empowering him in the matter of his religion.

Second: aiding him in repelling the oppression of the Jews and the disbelievers against him.

﴿You spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity﴾. As for his speaking to them in the cradle, it was specifically for informing them of his prophethood at that time. ﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive"﴾ [Maryam: 30–31]. As for his speaking to them in maturity, it was calling them to what Allah had commanded of prayer and zakah, and that was when he became thirty years old. Although he was sent as a prophet from the time he was born, he remained among them for thirty years, then Allah raised him. Allah did not send any prophet at birth other than him, and for this reason Allah singled him out with speaking in the cradle as an infant.
